title: G. Amulets
invariant: For any prefix of monsters and $k$ amulets, it is strictly optimal to grant immunity to the $k$ monster types with the largest accumulated damage in that prefix.
editorial_reduction:
Maintain two balanced heaps/sets partitioning monster types into the top-$k$ highest total damage and the remaining types.
As $k$ increases, dynamically advance the maximum defeatable prefix of monsters using two pointers.
Updating a monster's damage or balancing heaps takes $O(\log M)$ time per operation.

title: D. Two Signposts
invariant: A valid signpost orientation for each color forms a directed spanning tree rooted at that color's destination with no cycles, subject to the condition that no vertex points along the same directed edge in both trees.
editorial_reduction:
Construct the blue signposts by running DFS rooted at vertex 1, orienting edges towards the parent to establish a spanning tree directed to 1.
Construct yellow signposts via DFS rooted at vertex 2, enforcing the constraint that the yellow parent edge must not coincide with the blue parent edge.
If either DFS fails to visit all vertices, output No; otherwise, output the two valid parent pointer arrays.

title: F. Card Game
invariant: A graph represents a valid configuration of cards if and only if every connected component has at least 3 vertices or is a non-isolated edge structure without isolated $K_2$ components.
editorial_reduction:
Sort costs $C_i$ non-decreasingly and isolate vertex $N$ with the largest cost $C_{N-1}$.
Partition the remaining $N-1$ vertices into $k$ non-empty connected components, leaving $e = N - 1 - k$ surplus edges.
Evaluate the exact edge cost contribution: if $e \ge 2k$, surplus edges can be assigned cost $C_0$; otherwise, parity constraints require $(e \bmod 2) C_0$.
Minimize the total contribution across all $1 \le k \le N-1$ in $O(N)$ time using prefix sums.

title: G. Farthest City
invariant: The condition that vertex $N$ has strictly greater distance from vertex 1 than all other vertices implies $N$ is the unique vertex in the final layer $D$ of the BFS DAG.
editorial_reduction:
Define $dp[i][j]$ as the number of valid graph structures formed by placing $i$ intermediate vertices with the last layer containing $j$ vertices.
Transition by adding a new layer of $k$ vertices from the remaining unplaced labeled vertices: choose vertices with $\binom{N-1-i}{k}$, choose internal edges with $2^{k(k-1)/2}$, and connect each new vertex to at least one vertex in the previous layer with $(2^j - 1)^k$.
Finally, connect vertex $N$ to the last layer using $(2^j - 1)$ choices in $O(N^3)$ total time.

title: G. Count Grid 3-coloring
invariant: Since $H \times W \le 200$, transposing ensures $W \le 14$. The frontier profile of the last $W$ assigned cells completely determines validity of subsequent cell assignments.
editorial_reduction:
Transpose grid if $W > H$ so that $W \le 14$. Encode the boundary profile of the last $W$ cells using 2 bits per cell in an unsigned 32-bit integer.
Perform cell-by-cell broken profile dynamic programming across all $H \times W$ cells.
At each cell, verify color compatibility with top and left neighbors and update profiles via bit shifts and open-addressing hash aggregation.

title: C. Permutation Addition
invariant: Adding a permutation adds $N(N+1)/2$ to the total sum. A uniform state is achievable if and only if $\sum A_i \equiv 0 \pmod N$ for odd $N$, or $\sum A_i \in \{0, N/2\} \pmod N$ for even $N$.
editorial_reduction:
If $N$ is even and $\sum A_i \equiv N/2 \pmod N$, apply one standard permutation $(1, \dots, N)$ to reach $\sum A_i \equiv 0 \pmod N$.
Construct a pair of complementary permutations $(P_1, P_2)$ that transfers exactly 1 unit from the current maximum element index $u$ to the minimum element index $v$ while adding $N+1$ uniformly to all other positions.
Repeatedly transfer unit mass until all elements become equal, requiring at most $2 \times 2500 \le 5000$ operations.

title: G. Divide a Sequence
invariant: The product sum over partition blocks factors into $(\max(B) - \min(B)) dp[j] = \max(B) dp[j] - \min(B) dp[j]$, decoupling the maximum and minimum contributions independently.
editorial_reduction:
Maintain two monotonic stacks: one tracking non-increasing maximum values and one tracking non-decreasing minimum values alongside their accumulated $dp$ sums.
On inserting $A_i$, pop dominated elements while maintaining prefix sums $S_{\max}$ and $S_{\min}$ in $O(1)$ amortized time.
Compute $dp[i] = (S_{\max} - S_{\min}) \bmod 998244353$ in strictly linear $O(N)$ time.

title: F. Main Street
invariant: Any optimal trajectory between arbitrary grid points uses at most one entry and exit segment on regular streets to access the highway grid, projecting $S$ and $G$ onto their 4 bounding highway lines.
editorial_reduction:
Generate the 4 orthogonal projection points of $S$ onto adjacent highway grid lines $x = \lfloor S_x/B \rfloor B, \dots$ and similarly for $G$.
Compute shortest path distances along the regular highway grid between all $4 \times 4 = 16$ pairs of access points, taking detours into account if both points lie on the same cell boundary.
Take the minimum over all 16 highway paths and the direct regular street Manhattan distance.

title: F. substr = S
invariant: By linearity of occurrences, the total occurrences of $S$ in numbers $\le N$ equals the sum over all possible total lengths $D$ and starting offsets $p$ of the number of integers matching $S$ at position $p$.
editorial_reduction:
Express $\sum_{k=L}^R f(k) = \text{count}(R) - \text{count}(L-1)$.
For a fixed bound $N$, iterate over all possible digit lengths $D \le \text{len}(N)$ and starting positions $p \in [0, D - |S|]$.
Directly evaluate the number of valid prefixes and suffixes that keep the reconstructed number $\le N$ without full automaton construction.

title: F. Deforestation
invariant: For adjacent trees $(i, i+1)$, cutting $i$ before $i+1$ pays $H_{i+1}$, whereas cutting $i+1$ before $i$ pays $H_i$. Minimizing total cost imposes strict relative order constraints on adjacent cutting positions.
editorial_reduction:
Deduce that $H_i < H_{i+1}$ requires $pos[i] > pos[i+1]$, and $H_i > H_{i+1}$ requires $pos[i] < pos[i+1]$.
Use permutation insertion DP where $dp[j]$ tracks the number of permutations of prefix trees where the newest tree is placed at relative rank $j$.
Accelerate transitions across ranks using prefix sums to achieve $O(N^2)$ time.

title: D. Isomorphism Freak
invariant: A tree with minimum colorfulness must be completely symmetric with respect to either a central vertex (giving radius $D$, colorfulness $D+1$) or a central edge (giving radius $D$, colorfulness $D+1$).
editorial_reduction:
Iterate over all $N$ vertices as candidate centers, calculating maximum depth and maximum branch degrees at each distance level.
Iterate over all $N-1$ edges as candidate bicenters, rooting two symmetrical halves across the central bridge.
Minimize colorfulness first, and among ties minimize total leaf count $\prod \max(\text{degrees})$ in $O(N^2)$ time.

title: E. Snuke Line
topic: Splitting Objects into Light and Heavy / Case Processing
core_tags: Splitting Objects into Light and Heavy / Case Processing
invariant: Any interval of length $\ge d$ is guaranteed to contain at least one multiple of $d$. Intervals of length $< d$ contain at most one multiple of $d$ and can be queried via point evaluations.
editorial_reduction:
Sort and bucket intervals by their lengths $len_i = r_i - l_i + 1$.
As step size $d$ increases from $1$ to $M$, retire intervals with length $d - 1$ from the heavy count and insert them into a Fenwick tree (range add $[l_i, r_i]$).
Query all multiples $k \cdot d \le M$ in the Fenwick tree, yielding total complexity $O(N \log M + M \log^2 M)$.

title: C. ぬりまーす
invariant: Each Type 2 constraint $(u, v)$ requires either $u$ is painted before $v$ (adding directed edge $u \to v$) or $u$ is never painted (marking $u$ as forbidden).
editorial_reduction:
Since $B \le 10$, branch over all $2^B \le 1024$ assignments of Type 2 constraints.
For each assignment, construct the dependency graph with Type 1 edges $y \to x$ and Type 2 Choice 1 edges $u \to v$.
Propagate forbidden status to all reachable descendants, then run Kahn's topological sort on remaining vertices to detect and eliminate cycles, maximizing the number of painted vertices.

title: C. ビーム
invariant: Vertical beams restrict only X coordinates and horizontal beams restrict only Y coordinates, rendering movement costs along X and Y completely decoupled and independent.
editorial_reduction:
Decompose the problem into two independent 1D problems for $W$ and $H$.
In 1D, at each beam event time $t$, contiguous segments of attacked coordinates $[l, r]$ force any occupant to escape to $l-1$ or $r+1$ with distance cost.
Maintain $dp[x]$ dynamically, updating boundary positions and invalidating blocked cells in $O((W + H + Q) \log Q)$ time.

title: E. Black or White
invariant: Before either color is exhausted, each chocolate chosen is Black with probability $1/2$. Once White is exhausted, all remaining chocolates are Black with probability 1; once Black is exhausted, Black has probability 0.
editorial_reduction:
Express $P(i\text{-th is Black}) = 1/2 + 1/2 [P(\text{White exhausted before } i) - P(\text{Black exhausted before } i)]$.
The probability that White was exhausted in the first $n = i-1$ flips is the binomial tail $\sum_{k=W}^n \binom{n}{k} (1/2)^n$.
Update tail sums incrementally via $S(n) = S(n-1) + \binom{n-1}{W-1} (1/2)^n$ in $O(1)$ per step.

title: E. Three Substrings
invariant: Three strings $a, b, c$ can be embedded at relative offsets $(0, i, j)$ if and only if all three pairwise overlaps $(a, b)$ at $i$, $(a, c)$ at $j$, and $(b, c)$ at $j - i$ are mutually consistent.
editorial_reduction:
Precompute compatibility tables for each pair of strings over all relative shifts in $[-4000, 4000]$ in $O(|a||b| + |b||c| + |a||c|)$ time.
Iterate over valid shift offsets $(i, j) \in [-2000, 2000]^2$, pruning incompatible pairs in $O(1)$ via the precomputed table.
Compute the span $\max(|a|, i+|b|, j+|c|) - \min(0, i, j)$ and output the global minimum.
